---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Extractive Energy Provision"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Extractive energy provision covers natural gas, coal and petroleum. The account values it as the
resource rent each country earns from extraction, read from the World Bank's Changing Wealth of
Nations 2024 package at the GEP base year of 2019.

## Quantity and price

There is no separate quantity step and no separate price step. CWoN reports the rent itself, in
current USD per country per year, so the module reads that number and carries it through. The
price convention recorded for this service in `es_config.csv` is `resource rent`.

## Valuation

`fuel_rent_by_country_from_cwon` takes one CWoN table and returns one row per country holding the
`YR<year>` column at the requested year. The CWoN tables are wide, keyed on `countrycode` with
World Bank codes that match `iso3_r250_label` directly, Kosovo included as XKX.

`extractive_energy_gep_from_cwon` runs that read once per fuel and sums the three components with
`min_count=1`. A country absent from one fuel's table stays NaN in that component and still
receives a service total from the components that do exist, so a country with only coal is a coal
country rather than a missing one. Components sum by the same commodity convention that
extractive materials provision uses.

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, all scoped to the `extractive_energy` service:

- `extractive_energy_cwon_gas_path`, `extractive_energy_cwon_coal_path` and
  `extractive_energy_cwon_oil_path`, the Stata rent tables the valuation computes from. Each
  carries a `_source_url` row pointing at the World Bank reproducibility archive and a
  `_source_archive_member` row naming the file inside it, under
  `Reproducibility package/Output/Latest/`.
- `extractive_energy_gas_path`, `extractive_energy_coal_path` and `extractive_energy_oil_path`,
  the three committed per-country CSVs from the consortium drive, kept as the replication anchor.

The shared country references come from `initialize_country_paths`, which publishes the r264
correspondence and loads `p.df_countries`.

## Output

`gep_calculation` writes `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory. The columns
are the r250 identifiers and attributes, `year`, the three per-fuel columns
`extractive_energy_gas_gep`, `extractive_energy_coal_gep` and `extractive_energy_oil_gep`, and
their sum `extractive_energy_gep`.

## Method constants

`EXTRACTIVE_ENERGY_FUELS = ('gas', 'coal', 'oil')` names the three components and fixes the order
the summation reads them in.

`COMMITTED_DUPLICATE_VALUE_ROWS` records eight rows of the committed drive CSVs that carry another
country's full rent value. Bouvet Island and Svalbard take Norway's, Christmas Island and the
Cocos Islands take Australia's, Tokelau takes New Zealand's, Western Sahara takes Morocco's,
Palestine takes Israel's, and Kosovo takes Serbia's. In the Kosovo row the committed name column
itself reads "Serbia". The values were verified equal in every fuel where the row is non-empty.

## Taken as given

The CWoN rent estimation is upstream science and is used as published.

## What is open

The eight duplicate rows are a name-join artefact that counts the source countries twice, and for
Kosovo it overrides the CWoN table's own coal value. CWoN carries no rows at all for the first
six. The module therefore computes from the CWoN tables, one country one row, rather than
adopting the committed CSVs. `gep_calculation` logs the computed total beside the committed total
so the gap stays visible on every run.
